id-ag-2026-labrador-raul.name: Raul R. Labrador
id-ag-2026-labrador-raul.bio: Idaho Attorney General; former law firm owner, Idaho legislator, and eight-year U.S. Representative.

positions.stance: Has "fought to protect the unborn, keep men out of women's spaces and sports, and defended our state sovereignty."
Says he reformed Idaho's Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force to investigate predators and make arrests faster.
Believes "parents have the fundamental right to direct their children's education"; has defended Idaho's school choice tax credit.
Sued the Biden administration over border policies and supports the Trump administration in court on immigration enforcement and deportations.
Calls himself "a strong defender of our constitutional right to keep and bear arms" against federal overreach affecting law-abiding gun owners.

id-spi-2026-critchfield-debbie.name: Debbie Critchfield
id-spi-2026-critchfield-debbie.bio: Idaho Superintendent of Public Instruction since 2023; former Idaho State Board of Education president and Cassia County School Board member.

positions.stance: Pledges to lead Idaho education "with honesty, transparency, and wise solutions to empower parents, strengthen local control, and prepare our students for the workforce."
Lists "Back to the Basics" as a priority, including returning reading instruction to phonics.
Lists "Protect and Promote American Values" as a priority, citing new U.S. history, government, and civics standards.
Lists "Prepare Students with Life Skills" as a priority, citing required financial and digital literacy classes and expanded career-technical education.

id-spi-2026-sundin-mitchell-becky.name: Becky Sundin Mitchell
id-spi-2026-sundin-mitchell-becky.bio: Educator with more than 20 years teaching grades 6-12 science and English in Idaho charter and public schools; holds a Doctor of Education.

positions.stance: Says school funding reform "should prioritize student needs, including support for rural schools, CTE programs, and special education funding."
Supports strengthening teacher recruitment, retention, and compensation to keep high-quality teachers in Idaho classrooms.
"Funding should not follow political trends"; notes Idaho ranks near the bottom in per-pupil spending despite over $1 billion in reserves.
Supports investing in early literacy, evidence-based instruction, and targeted interventions so every student reads at grade level.
Wants every student, "regardless of background, ability, or zip code," to have academic, behavioral, and mental health support.

ri-sos-2026-amore-gregg.name: Gregg M. Amore
ri-sos-2026-amore-gregg.bio: Rhode Island Secretary of State; former East Providence High School history teacher and state representative.

positions.stance: "Rhode Islanders believe in fair elections, transparent government, and a democracy that works for everyone"; cites expanding ballot access and modernizing government services.

ri-ag-2026-gordon-alan.name: Alan Leonard Gordon
ri-ag-2026-gordon-alan.bio: Holds an Honors LL.B. from the University of Buckingham and has provided private legal guidance to Christian organizations on ecclesiastical law since 2014.

positions.stance: Pledges to apply "the same evidentiary and legal standards regardless of political affiliation" and seek independent review when conflicted.
"I will not prosecute women seeking abortions"; would enforce laws against those who exploit, coerce, or endanger women and children.
Will defend the constitutional rights of "Christians, Jews, Muslims, members of every faith, and those with no religious affiliation" equally.
Will seek appointment of truly independent counsel when the Attorney General's Office has a genuine conflict of interest.
Will challenge firearm restrictions he considers unconstitutional, "including magazine bans, so-called 'assault weapon' bans, unjustified age restrictions."

ri-ag-2026-ahern-kimberly.name: Kimberly Ahern
ri-ag-2026-ahern-kimberly.bio: Former Rhode Island prosecutor, counselor to two governors and three attorneys general, and state regulator.

positions.stance: Will put "the criminal prosecution unit front-and-center, aggressively prosecute violent offenders, stand up for victims."
Will expand diversion programs connecting people with mental illness and addiction to treatment while still holding individuals accountable.
Will "vigorously enforce our civil rights laws, strengthen hate crime prevention and prosecution," and give law enforcement tools and training.
Will take the Trump administration to court "when it oversteps its authority or puts our residents at risk."
Will defend Rhode Island's law codifying Roe v. Wade and protect "access to reproductive health care, privacy, and dignity for all."

ri-treas-2026-credle-micholas.name: Micholas A. Credle
ri-treas-2026-credle-micholas.bio: Retired U.S. Army captain and executive financial consultant; founder of Collegiate Compass.

positions.stance: Calls for examining the impact of the 2011 pension reforms and "a sustainable path toward restoring meaningful cost-of-living adjustments."
Wants the Treasurer's Office to promote financial education and partnerships supporting veteran housing and long-term financial stability.
Will scrutinize investment-management and consultant fees, contracts, and performance, judging pension dollars "on measurable net returns."
Says Treasury information such as pension performance, fees, and contracts "should be understandable to every resident, not just insiders."
Will modernize unclaimed-property operations with proactive identification and outreach to return money to its owners.

ri-treas-2026-diossa-james.name: James A. Diossa
ri-treas-2026-diossa-james.bio: Rhode Island General Treasurer; former mayor of Central Falls.

de-ag-2026-jennings-kathy.name: Kathy Jennings
de-ag-2026-jennings-kathy.bio: Delaware Attorney General; former State Prosecutor, Chief Deputy Attorney General, and New Castle County Chief Administrative Officer.

de-ag-2026-graham-david.name: David C. "Dave" Graham
de-ag-2026-graham-david.bio: U.S. Army veteran (E-5 sergeant), retired senior executive, and CDL-A driver.

positions.stance: "Prioritize serious and violent crime and bring greater accountability and transparency to prosecution decisions."
Build a stronger working relationship between the Department of Justice and Delaware's state and local law-enforcement agencies.
Address critical staffing needs, recruit and retain qualified prosecutors, and bring effective management and accountability to DOJ operations.
Protect Delawareans from fraud, scams, and deceptive practices while ensuring crime victims "are heard, protected and treated with respect."
"Bring transparency, responsible leadership and fair and consistent enforcement of the law to Delaware's Department of Justice."

de-aud-2026-york-lydia.name: Lydia York
de-aud-2026-york-lydia.bio: Delaware State Auditor; attorney and certified public accountant.

positions.stance: Her office works with schools, districts, and the Department of Education "to ensure school funding supports our children, and is managed responsibly."
Committed to "investigating and reporting on inefficient spending and the misuse of your tax dollars" and working to recover funds.
Says her office publishes more audit reports than ever, "helping our government better serve everyone in Delaware."

de-aud-2026-callaway-april.name: April Callaway
de-aud-2026-callaway-april.bio: Insurance and billing administrator for a local dental group for 18 years.

positions.stance: Will publicly identify who is responsible when audits are obstructed and use the office's authority to ensure problems are fixed.
Would audit every school district so districts are not "in the red and unduly raising property taxes."
Says audits "should be written so a taxpayer can read them and understand what happened to their money."
Would have the Auditor's office itself audited every two years and make the results public.

de-treas-2026-lauzen-ted.name: Ted Lauzen
de-treas-2026-lauzen-ted.bio: Investment manager, business owner, combat veteran, and Board Treasurer of the Delaware YMCA.

positions.stance: Will protect Delaware's AAA credit rating and update state debt policies so the state can borrow more efficiently.
Will expand access to financial literacy and savings programs "like the DE 529, the EARNS program, and the ABLE plan."
Will partner with Delaware's 57 towns and municipalities on best practices to "reduce the fees we pay to Wall Street."
Will lead investment oversight and transparency efforts to ensure public funds are used appropriately and reduce waste.
Will serve on the Board of Pardons with "an experienced and empathetic approach" that can offer Delawareans "a second chance."

de-treas-2026-ramone-michael.name: Michael Ramone
de-treas-2026-ramone-michael.bio: Businessman and entrepreneur; former Delaware House Minority Leader.

positions.stance: Says Delaware's corporate franchise system is a major revenue source whose "stability cannot be taken for granted."
"Delaware needs a Treasurer who puts fiscal responsibility ahead of political agendas" to keep borrowing costs low.
"The State Treasurer should be the taxpayers' independent watchdog—not the Governor's accountant."
Pledges to "hold regular news conferences and public forums" so taxpayers know where their money goes.
Will protect Delaware EARNS, DE 529, and DE ABLE "from unnecessary political interference" and ensure programs deliver results.

sd-sos-2026-baxter-heather.name: Heather Baxter
sd-sos-2026-baxter-heather.bio: South Dakota state representative for District 34 since 2024 and small business owner in Rapid City and Custer.

positions.stance: Will implement robust and secure practices "to ensure every vote is counted accurately via paper ballots."
Will work with legislators on campaign finance reform, "fostering trust through clear, open reporting."
Advocates an "SD DOGE" to simplify regulations and streamline processes for entrepreneurs.
Pledges to "lead with steadfast dedication to the people of South Dakota" with integrity and reliability.
Plans "to further improve public access to records with modern, user-friendly tools."

sd-sos-2026-davis-terrence.name: Terrence Davis
sd-sos-2026-davis-terrence.bio: Former state trooper in Tennessee and South Dakota who most recently worked at East River Legal Services.

positions.stance: Keep "the tested, audited ballot counters we use today, with people checking the results."
Let 16-year-olds pre-register when they get a driver's license, and keep voting close to home, especially in rural counties.
Says voters' personal details "deserve real protection" and that "Privacy gets built into every system from the start."
Create an investigative division inside the office to look into fraud so real problems are found and fixed quickly.
Make filing with the state "simple, fast, and friendly" for businesses and nonprofits.

sd-ag-2026-russell-lance.name: Lance Russell
sd-ag-2026-russell-lance.bio: Longtime State's Attorney for Fall River County and Oglala Lakota County.

sd-aud-2026-barranco-catherine.name: Catherine Barranco
sd-aud-2026-barranco-catherine.bio: Former investigator in the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's Office of Internet Enforcement and credit union title/lien auditor.

positions.stance: As State Auditor, "I will work to identify savings, improve government efficiency, and create opportunities for tax relief."

sd-treas-2026-hull-melissa.name: Melissa Hull
sd-treas-2026-hull-melissa.bio: Has worked in the South Dakota State Treasurer's Office for eight years; small business owner.

positions.stance: "Committed to transparency and accountability with taxpayer dollars."
Pledges "clear oversight and strong accountability voters expect."

sd-treas-2026-kuipers-margaret.name: Margaret Kuipers
sd-treas-2026-kuipers-margaret.bio: Business owner who served 14 years as state treasurer of the South Dakota Emergency Medical Services Association.

positions.stance: Running "to protect the state's assets with integrity, accountability and responsible financial oversight."
"I will be a responsible and transparent steward of the state's finances, making sure every tax dollar is accounted for."

sd-spl-2026-mettler-raeann.name: Raeann Mettler
sd-spl-2026-mettler-raeann.bio: Scientist, educator, researcher, and small business owner from Spearfish.

positions.stance: Generate additional revenue for public education by improving land use management and streamlining the purchase and sale of property.
Protect "the natural landscapes, native species, and water quality on public lands" and maintain access for responsible recreational use.
Improve accountability and transparency by prioritizing public input and expanding how the office communicates with the public.

sd-puc-2026-haggar-don.name: Don Haggar
sd-puc-2026-haggar-don.bio: Small business owner; former South Dakota House member (2013-2020) and Speaker Pro Tem, and former state director of Americans for Prosperity.

positions.stance: "Fight costly mandates and overregulation while promoting competition to reduce prices."
Defend landowner rights by "opposing government overreach and eminent domain abuse."
"Prioritize grid stability with smart investments and strengthened infrastructure to handle peak demand and weather extremes."
Opposes "any data center development that leaves South Dakotans with higher bills, fewer resources, or less control over their own communities."
Would "oppose pipelines and demand transparency, accountability, and full respect" for affected landowners.
Committed "to fighting against unjustified rate increases" and scrutinizing every proposal.
Will advocate policies that protect residents "from predatory practices" and ensure they receive the quality service they pay for.
Will "champion the rights of farmers, landowners, and small towns" and resist measures that disproportionately impact rural areas.

nd-sos-2026-howe-michael.name: Michael Howe
nd-sos-2026-howe-michael.bio: North Dakota Secretary of State since 2022; former Howe Seed Farms managing partner and six-year state representative.

positions.stance: Supports "the most secure and transparent elections in the nation while keeping them accessible for every eligible voter," including proof of citizenship and paper ballots.
Will keep North Dakota a top place to do business "by continuing to cut red tape and support a pro-business environment."
Committed to managing educational trusts, mineral acres, and other assets "responsibly and efficiently" for future generations.

nd-agr-2026-goehring-doug.name: Doug Goehring
nd-agr-2026-goehring-doug.bio: North Dakota Agriculture Commissioner since 2009 and farmer near Menoken.
